explanations.title: L8 Take from the ones or from a ten
explanations.text: Look at the ones. If you have enough ones, take from the ones. If not, take from a ten.

explanations.title: L8 Take from a ten within 100
explanations.text: To take 8 from 23, break 23 into 13 and 10. 10 minus 8 equals 2. Then 13 plus 2 equals 15.

assets_required.why_this_method: Needs exact numbers in fixed circles and a hidden part. This is layout and behaviour, not a picture.
assets_required.description: A number bond: one circle on top (the total) joined by lines to two circles below (the parts). One circle can show a question mark.
must_show_exactly: Total circle on top, two part circles below
Known numbers shown; the missing part shows a question mark
Numbers and any missing part match the current lesson question stimulus.
states_or_frames: configured from the current lesson question stimulus
assets_required.interaction: Shows the bond. The child answers by typing or speaking. The missing part is revealed after the answer.
assets_required.alt_text: A number bond with a total on top and two parts below.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat number bond: one big circle on top joined by two lines to two smaller circles below, plain background, numbers set by the question. [Build by code]

review_flags.issue: Card is a DRAFT made by an AI. Not reviewed. A person must review it before any use.
Source license is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (Great Minds). Cards made from it must credit Great Minds, stay non-commercial, and share under the same license. Check before any paid deployment.
Build the 1 lesson visual specifications by code and check exact quantities against each rubric.
Lesson 8 was extracted by lesson-specific IDs. Its objective and scoped asset states are adapted. Review them against the original lesson before use.

The source is 8 markdown files with no printed page numbers, no images and no 'This file derived from' footer. Every page is 'n/a' with a section name. source_version is 'not_stated_in_file' and source_refs holds one item for the whole zip. Fill both in from the original PDFs.

The worksheets have no printed titles in these files. They were named by order after the Exit Ticket instructions: Lessons 1 to 3 start with Sprint A and Sprint B. Lessons 3 to 8 then show Problem Set, Exit Ticket, Homework. Lessons 1 and 2 show Exit Ticket, Homework. A person must confirm this against the PDFs. Section names that say Problem Set, Exit Ticket or Homework depend on it.
The source is a teacher script for a class with a Rekenrek, cards and partners. All child text was rewritten for a screen. Needs age-appropriate wording review.

ext_g1_add_subtract_within_10, ext_k_say_ten_counting and ext_g1_place_value_tens_ones are external prerequisite cards that do not exist yet. The source names Grade 1 and Kindergarten work as earlier learning but does not teach it.

The source prints no answers for Sprints, Exit Tickets, Homework or Problem Sets, and none for most Fluency and word-problem items. Every such key is derived. Each was solved by code from the printed item, then checked against the lesson text.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
